correctness.rationale: The maximum path eigenvalue is simple and has a nowhere-zero eigenvector. The critical Jacobian is a sum of two PSD matrices, singular only at the all-pi point; a strict integral monotonicity inequality proves global injectivity and degree-one topology gives surjectivity. A quartic coercivity inequality proves inverse Hölder 1/3 and the nonzero cubic coefficient along the kernel proves optimality. Analytic Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction yields exactly three local roots and the explicit sqrt excess-step amplitude. Critical-map injectivity plus torus compactness excludes other global preimages. Sink persistence follows from 0<h<2/λ. Standalone finite checker verifies spectral and branch diagnostics but is not used as an infinite proof.
